blocks.text: ZDX allows you to manage your collections to easily organize your applications and probes.
The difference between the configuration steps for managing collections for End User and Managed users depends on where the collections are located:

blocks.item: End User Monitoring page: Digital Experience > Settings & Configurations > Probes > End User
Managed Monitoring page: Digital Experience > Settings & Configurations > Probes > Managed

blocks.text: You can manage your collections with the following actions:

blocks.item: Adding a collection.
You can add a collection using the following steps:
End User
On the End User Monitoring page:
Click Add Collection.
The Add End User Collection drawer appears.
See image.
Configure the following:
Under End User Collection Settings:
Name: Enter the name of the collection.
Status: Click to enable or disable the collection.
Tags: (Optional) Select or create tags for the collection to easily identify your collection.
Description: (Optional) Enter a description of the collection.
Click Next.
Under Exclusion Criteria and Probing Criteria, you can configure policies for the following criteria:
User Groups
Users
Location Groups
Zscaler Locations
Departments
Devices
OS
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Probing Criteria Logic.
Any application under the collection follows the collection's probing criteria instead of its own probing criteria.
Click Next.
Click Add.
Managed
On the Managed Monitoring page:
Click Add Collection.
The Add Managed Collection drawer appears.
See image.
Configure the following:
Name: Enter the name of the collection.
Status: Toggle to enable or disable the collection.
Tags: (Optional) Select or create tags for the collection to easily identify your collection.
Description: (Optional) Enter a description of the collection.
Click Add.
Editing the collection.
You can edit a collection using the following steps:
End User
On the End User Monitoring page:
Under Actions, click Edit on the collection you want to edit.
The Edit End User Collection drawer appears.
See image.
Configure the fields as needed. These are the same configurable fields when you add the collection.
Click Next.
Click Update.
Managed
On the Managed Monitoring page:
Under Actions, click Edit on the collection you want to edit.
The Edit Managed Collection drawer appears.
See image.
Configure the fields as needed. These are the same configurable fields when you add the collection.
Click Next.
Click Update.
Deleting the collection.

Deleting a collection means you are also removing any applications and their associated probes under the collection. If you delete an End User collection where the application is in multiple collections, the application is only removed from that deleted collection.
The Delete action is similar for both the End User Monitoring and Managed Monitoring pages.
For Managed Monitoring, you must delete the probes attached to an application before you can delete a collection.
To delete a collection:
Under Actions, click Delete on the collection you want to delete.
On the Deletion window, click Delete to confirm deletion.
You cannot delete the default collections (i.e., Unified Communication Collection, Predefined Apps Collection, Custom Apps Collection).
Removing an application from an End User Collection.

You can remove an application from an End User collection. You cannot remove an application from the Unified Communication Collection. You cannot remove an application from Predefined Apps Collection if its status is Pending Onboard.
To remove an application:
Go to the collection where you want to remove the application.
Under Actions, click Remove from Collection on the application you want to remove.
On the Remove App from Collection window, click Remove to confirm the removal.
Activate the changes.
Ranking collections on the End User Monitoring page.
On the End User Monitoring page, you can drag and drop customized collections to rank them for priority.
You cannot change the rankings of the default End User collections (e.g., Predefined Apps Collection).
Disabling or enabling within a collection.
You can enable or disable the following on either the End User Monitoring or Managed Monitoring pages:
Collections: On the collection you want to update, toggle to enable or disable the collection.
Applications: On the application you want to update, toggle to enable or disable the application.
Probes: On the probe you want to update, edit the probe to toggle its status.
After any change in the status, you must activate the changes.

If you disable a collection, then you disable any applications within it. For End User collections, if the application is in another collection, then the application is only disabled for the disabled collection.

If you disable an application, then you disable all the probes associated with it. For End User collections, if the application is in another collection, then the application is disabled for all collections.

Adding a custom application.
Editing an application.
Deleting the application.
To delete an application:
End User

For End User Monitoring, you can delete an application from a custom collection or the Custom Apps Collection. You cannot delete an application from the Unified Communication Collection or the Predefined Apps Collection.
Prior to deleting an application, you must delete its corresponding probes.
To delete an application for End User Monitoring:
Go to the collection where the application resides that you want to delete.
Under Actions, click Delete.
On the Deletion window, click Delete to confirm the deletion.
Managed
For the Managed Monitoring page, you must delete the probe before you can delete an application.
After you have deleted the probe, you can delete the application on the Managed Monitoring page:
Go to the collection where the application resides that you want to delete.
Under Actions, click Delete.
On the Deletion window, click Delete to confirm the deletion.

blocks.text: Consider the following when you manage collections:

blocks.item: To remove probes, you must either delete the collection or delete the application. You cannot delete probes by themselves.
For End User collections:
If you remove the application from a collection, then it is only removed for that collection.
If the application is in multiple collections, then there are rankings. To learn more, see Understanding Collections.
For Managed collections, you can configure an application for only one collection. Therefore, if you remove the application from a collection, it also removes all the associated probes.
The number of applications and probes you can configure depends on your subscription level. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
